sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the northern end of Bergenfield at 50 feet to an inch, from Maple on the Dumont borough line at the top (the area beyond is marked "See Map of Dumont") south to East and West Central Avenue. The tracks of the West Shore Railroad run down the west edge. Caroline Street and North Washington Avenue are the north-south streets; West and East Kipp Avenue, Maria, Merritt Avenue and Tuscarora cross them, and Leonard, New Jersey Avenue and New York Avenue appear at the east edge. The blocks between the railroad and Caroline Street and between Caroline Street and Washington Avenue are laid out in numbered lots with only a few dwellings, and a large open tract south of Maria holds the B.P.O.E. Lodge No. 1477 and a group of greenhouses with a potting house. Washington Avenue is the commercial strip, with several auto repairing and storage garages, an auto service station, a filling station and an auto washing shed, mostly of cinder block. Frame dwellings fill the blocks east of Washington Avenue between Merritt Avenue and East Central Avenue. Churches are the Evangelical Lutheran St. Matthew's Church on Tuscarora and All Saints Church (Episcopal) with its rectory on West Central Avenue. A 24-inch water main follows Washington Avenue, with 6-inch pipes in the cross streets.
notes: Maple, on the Dumont borough line, is now Columbia Avenue.
Leonard is now Slater Street.
East Kipp Avenue is now Kipp Avenue.
The West Shore Railroad (W.S.R.R.) runs along the west edge; today the line is CSX's River Subdivision.
B.P.O.E. Lodge No. 1477 stands in the open block south of Maria Street.

50 ft. North end: Maple (now Columbia Avenue, Dumont line), Caroline, W/E Kipp, Maria, N Washington, Merritt, Tuscarora, W/E Central, Home Pl, Leonard (now Slater St); West Shore RR at west edge. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers central Bergenfield north of the business centre, at 50 feet to an inch, between East Central Avenue at the top and De Mott Avenue at the bottom. The tracks of the West Shore Railroad run down the west edge, with North Railroad Avenue beside them. North Washington Avenue crosses the sheet from top to bottom slightly right of centre; west of it are Home Place and Irving Place, crossed by Simone Place, West Johnson Avenue and Annex Place, and east of it Hickory Avenue, East Johnson Avenue, Bond and North William run to the east edge. Much of the west half is laid out in numbered lots that are still largely vacant, especially the large blocks beside the railroad. The civic buildings of the borough stand on Washington Avenue: Borough Hall with Fire Department Company No. 2, and a K. of C. Hall on the east side north of Hickory Avenue. Washington Avenue also has a hotel at West Johnson Avenue, auto repairing and auto wrecking shops, an upholstering shop and filling stations. The blocks east of Washington Avenue and along Irving Place carry scattered frame dwellings with garages. A 24-inch water main runs along Washington Avenue and 6- and 8-inch pipes in the cross streets. The bottom strip along De Mott Avenue, with Short Street, is repeated on sheet 5.
notes: Borough Hall and Fire Department Company No. 2 stand on Washington Avenue between Simone Place and West Johnson Avenue.
Bond, at the east edge, could not be matched to a modern street and was not used for control.
The West Shore Railroad (W.S.R.R.) runs along the west edge; today the line is CSX's River Subdivision.
50 ft. E Central to De Mott: Home Pl, Simone Pl, N Washington, Hickory, W/E Johnson, Irving Pl, Annex Pl, N Railroad Av; Borough Hall. Bond (east edge) not matched. One part.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the west side of the Bergenfield business centre around the railroad station, at 50 feet to an inch. It runs from West Church Street at the top to Froelich Street at the bottom, and from North and South Demarest Avenue on the west edge across the tracks of the West Shore Railroad to Station Square, North and South Railroad Avenue and Portland Avenue on the east. Tyson Place, West Main Street and Van Houten Street cross the blocks between Demarest Avenue and North and South Front Street, which runs along the west side of the tracks; Ralph Street and Arlington Avenue meet Church and Froelich Streets. The passenger depot stands on the east side of the tracks with Station Square beside it, and a freight house lies on the west side further south. Along the tracks are the yard and sheds of Christie and Terhune, mason's supplies (lath, lime and cement storage and mason's materials). West Main Street near the railroad is commercial, with a bank and a post office of tile construction, brick stores and offices; an auto repair shop stands on West Church Street and a plumber on Tyson Place. The remaining blocks hold frame dwellings and garages on narrow numbered lots, with a few vacant lots along Froelich Street. Six-inch water pipes run in the cross streets.
notes: The passenger depot of the West Shore Railroad (W.S.R.R.) stands on Station Square; today the line is CSX's River Subdivision and Station Square corresponds to Veterans Plaza.
Christie and Terhune mason's supplies occupy the strip along the east side of the tracks south of West Main Street.
A bank and the post office stand on West Main Street west of the railroad.
50 ft. W Church to Froelich, N/S Demarest to Portland Av across the railroad; Tyson Pl, W Main, Van Houten, N/S Front, depot and Station Sq (now Veterans Plaza). One part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the business centre of Bergenfield around the bend of Washington Avenue, at 50 feet to an inch. It runs from De Mott Avenue and Irving Place at the top to below Main Street at the bottom, and from North Railroad Avenue and Station Square on the west (the railroad itself lies just off the sheet, on sheet 4) to North and South William Street on the east edge. Washington Avenue enters at the top as a straight north-south street, bends south-west below Church Street and continues as South Washington Avenue towards sheet 6. West Church and East Church meet Washington Avenue at offset corners, and Bradley Avenue runs east from Washington Avenue to William Street. The densest building is along Washington Avenue between Church and Main Streets and along South Washington Avenue below Main Street: rows of brick stores, a bank at the Main Street corner, a bakery with a portable oven, a factory and plumbers' shops, with frame dwellings and garages on the side streets. St. John's Roman Catholic Church, its convent and St. John's Parochial School occupy the block between Bradley Avenue, Main Street and William Street. A wood works stands on East Church Street near William Street. West of Washington Avenue, between North Railroad Avenue, Short Street and De Mott Avenue, lots are laid out but mostly unbuilt. Water pipes are drawn in most streets, including a 24-inch main along the north part of Washington Avenue.
notes: George is now Legion Drive.
Station Square, between Church and Main Streets beside the railroad, corresponds to today's Veterans Plaza.
William north of East Church is today Bell Place; the junction drawn there was left out as it fits the modern node poorly (7 m).
A 24-inch water main runs along North Washington Avenue.
50 ft. Business centre: De Mott to below Main, N Railroad Av to William; Short, W/E Church, Bradley, Washington bend, George (now Legion Drive). Pilot sheet. One part.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the southern part of Bergenfield's business district along South Washington Avenue, at 50 feet to an inch, from below Main Street at the top to East and West Clinton Avenue at the bottom. The West Shore Railroad runs along the west edge with South Railroad Avenue beside it; Portland Avenue and South Washington Avenue run north-south, crossed by Bedford Avenue, Delford Avenue and West Clinton Avenue on the west and by Palisade Avenue, Bergen Avenue, Madison Avenue and East Clinton Avenue on the east, where George and James streets reach the edge. South Washington Avenue is lined with brick and cinder-block stores, among them a drug store, a bakery, a lunch room, a furniture store and a battery service. Larger works and public buildings cluster on its west side: the Palace Theatre (motion pictures), the Foerster Baking Co. Inc. bakery, the Public Service bus garage, a garage with auto sales and service on Delford Avenue, and the Blue Moon Ice Cream Co. Inc. plant. The R. J. Muller & Co. lumber yard and lumber warehouse stand near the railroad at the north-west, with a sign painting shop further south. East of Washington Avenue are an auto repair shop and the Bergenfield Calendar Mfg. Co. printing works on Palisade Avenue, an Episcopal church near East Clinton Avenue, and blocks of frame dwellings with garages. A 24-inch water main runs along Washington Avenue.
notes: Madison Avenue is also labelled Mulligan in parentheses.
George is now Legion Drive.
The Washington Avenue / Clinton Avenue junction was left out: Clinton Avenue has been widened (about 81 ft today) and the junction fits 9 m off.
R. J. Muller & Co. lumber yard, Foerster Baking Co., the Palace Theatre, the Public Service bus garage, Blue Moon Ice Cream Co. and Bergenfield Calendar Mfg. Co. are on this sheet.
50 ft. S Washington from below Main to Clinton: Bedford, Portland, Delford, Palisade, Bergen, Madison (Mulligan), James, George. One part.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the area south of Clinton Avenue on both sides of South Washington Avenue, at 50 feet to an inch, from West and East Clinton Avenue at the top to Terhune and East Broad Street at the bottom. The tracks of the West Shore Railroad touch the north-west corner. West of Washington Avenue most of the sheet is one large open block (block 107), almost empty except for the Harding Public School near Clinton Avenue, a fireproof school with an auditorium, a stage and a gymnasium, and a few dwellings along Washington Avenue. Below it School Street and Terhune Street bound partly built residential blocks with frame dwellings. East of Washington Avenue, Edward Street and O'Neill Street run across to Smith Avenue at the east edge; these blocks are filled with frame dwellings and garages on narrow lots, many of them recently built. Commercial buildings are few: an auto repairing shop with a show room on Terhune Street and a cinder-block garage with a parts room and show room at the corner of Washington Avenue and East Broad Street, with cinder-block stores nearby. A 24-inch water main runs along Washington Avenue and 6- and 8-inch pipes in the cross streets.
notes: O'Neill is spelled O Neil Street in OpenStreetMap.
The Harding Public School stands in the large open block west of Washington Avenue.
50 ft. Clinton to Terhune/E Broad: Harding Public School in open block 107; Edward, O'Neill, Smith Av, School St. One part.

sheet-8-1.description: Sheet 8, part 1, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the north-west corner of Bergenfield between the Dumont line at the top and Riveredge Road at the bottom, with North Prospect Avenue along the east edge. Most of the sheet is a newly laid-out residential tract: Woods Avenue, Harrington Street, North Vivyen Street, Elder Avenue and Ames Avenue run north-south across Williamson Road and down to Riveredge Road, and Beverly Place, Berwyn Place, Brewster Place and Banta Place run east from Ames Avenue. Lots are numbered and many are still vacant; scattered frame dwellings with garages stand on them, with a few brick-veneered houses on Elder Avenue and one frame-and-concrete building on North Vivyen Street. A block of frame dwellings lines both sides of Banta Place near North Prospect Avenue. The upper half of the sheet is largely open ground: the Bergenfield and Dumont Sewerage Disposal Plant occupies a large walled area of filter beds, with an underground settling basin and gate house. Along North Prospect Avenue a row of deep lots holds frame dwellings and a set of greenhouses, with Maple Street and West Central Avenue leaving to the east; a fire alarm box stands at West Central Avenue. Six-inch water pipes run in North Prospect Avenue, Harrington Street, Banta Place and Riveredge Road. North Stoughton Street and Jones Place appear only as labels at the foot of the sheet. The top left corner of the sheet holds a separate inset (part 2).
notes: Maple Street is now Columbia Avenue (junction with North Prospect Avenue fits at 0.4 m).
Riveredge Road is "River Edge Road" in OpenStreetMap; West Central Avenue meets North Prospect Avenue at the node named Central Avenue.
Williamson Road today continues east of Ames Avenue as a loop to Brewster Place; on the sheet it ends at Ames Avenue. That modern junction was excluded.
Bergenfield and Dumont Sewerage Disposal Plant (filter beds, settling basin, gate house) occupies the upper middle of the sheet.
100 ft. North-west: Williamson Rd, Woods, Harrington, N. Vivyen, Elder, Ames, Riveredge Rd, N. Prospect, sewage disposal plant. Part 2: boxed inset top left, Armour Pl at N. Prospect (Dumont line).

sheet-8-2.description: Sheet 8, part 2 is a small inset in the top left corner of the sheet, boxed off by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch, showing the strip of Bergenfield north of the main sheet along the Dumont line. It covers two blocks either side of Armour Place, which runs west from North Prospect Avenue; the dash-dot borough line runs along the top and down the west side, with the note "See Map of Dumont" beyond it. Narrow lots, numbered 1 to 38 in blocks 2 and 3, front Armour Place; most are vacant. A handful of dwellings stand on them, all frame except one of concrete block, with a chicken coop and small garages. On the east side of North Prospect Avenue the inset shows only the mouths of Quackenbush Avenue and Erie Street, with a town hydrant near Quackenbush. A six-inch water pipe runs in North Prospect Avenue. The sheet's compass rose and the key number 401 lie just below the inset on the main part.
notes: North Prospect Avenue here is "Prospect Avenue" in OpenStreetMap (the Dumont section); Quackenbush Avenue is West Quackenbush Avenue.

Only one junction (Armour Place / Prospect Avenue) was detected; Erie Street and Quackenbush Avenue, which meet North Prospect Avenue from the east, were hand-picked. All three points lie along one street, so the part is placed by a helmert fit and its rotation rests on North Prospect Avenue alone.
The inset is bounded by the Dumont line; the area beyond is drawn on the Dumont map.
100 ft. North-west: Williamson Rd, Woods, Harrington, N. Vivyen, Elder, Ames, Riveredge Rd, N. Prospect, sewage disposal plant. Part 2: boxed inset top left, Armour Pl at N. Prospect (Dumont line).

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the northern part of Bergenfield between North Prospect Avenue on the west and the West Shore Railroad on the east, from Maple Avenue at the Dumont line (the borough boundary, with "See Map of Dumont" beyond) down to Cleveland Street. The upper third is a newly platted tract: blocks 46B to 46E of narrow numbered lots along Maple Avenue, Stillman Avenue and Blauvelt Avenue, cut by Walters Street, Blackwell Street and Dick Street; only the block between Stillman and Blauvelt east of Blackwell is built up, with a row of frame dwellings. Below Blauvelt Avenue long deep lots run down to West Central Avenue, with scattered frame dwellings and a few concrete-block and stucco houses. South of West Central Avenue are Pelham Place, Cooper Street, Ann Street, Carlisle Street, Ralph Street and the start of North Demarest Avenue, lined with frame dwellings and some brick-veneered and tile houses. The south-west quarter is open ground with a swamp and a large pond on a stream that flows out at the foot of the sheet; a wood-working shop with a water wheel stands at the pond's north end, and the Virgil Piano School Co. works (manufacturing dummy pianos, with a two-storey finishing building) lies east of it. The Mayone Co. of N.J. mason materials yard, with a hoisting engine and storage shed, adjoins the railroad at the top right. North Railroad Avenue, Annex Place, De Mott Avenue and West Johnson Street are shown only at the east edge beyond the tracks. Water pipes of 6 inches run in most streets.
notes: Maple Avenue (the Dumont boundary) is now Columbia Avenue.
Riveredge Road is "River Edge Road" and Cooper's Lane is "Cooper Lane" in OpenStreetMap.
The Dick Street / Blauvelt Avenue junction fits 5 m off and Ralph Street / Central Avenue 4.7 m: Dick Street bends here and both are accepted at the edge of the tolerance.
Virgil Piano School Co. (manufacturing dummy pianos), a wood-working shop with water wheel on the pond, and the Mayone Co. of N.J. mason materials yard are on this sheet.
100 ft. North, N. Prospect to the railroad, Maple Av (Dumont line) to Cleveland St; pond, Virgil Piano School Co., Mayone mason yard.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the western part of Bergenfield between Riveredge Road at the top and a line below Vreeland Avenue, from beyond North and South Queen Street on the west to North and South Prospect Avenue on the east. It is a regular grid of streets laid out ahead of building. North of West Main Street, Woods Avenue, Harrington Street, North Vivyen Street, Elder Avenue, Ames Avenue and North Stoughton Street run north-south across Graphic Boulevard, a 70-foot boulevard, with James Place, Kathryn Place and the end of West Church Street near North Prospect Avenue; the large blocks 17B to 18I are almost entirely vacant, with only a few frame dwellings and a house foundation near Ames Avenue and North Stoughton Street. South of West Main Street the blocks between Harcourt Avenue, Reid Avenue and Vreeland Avenue, crossed by South Queen Street, South Vivyen Street and Stoughton Place, are divided into narrow numbered lots and partly built up with rows of small frame dwellings, mostly one- and two-storey, with garages behind; one dwelling is of brick veneer and two cinder-block buildings stand near West Main Street at North Prospect Avenue. The bottom of the sheet (block 21D) is open ground. Six- and eight-inch water pipes run in Riveredge Road, Harcourt Avenue, Reid Avenue and the Prospect avenues. The compass rose and scale are at the lower right; the area east of South Prospect Avenue belongs to sheet 11.
notes: James Place is now Jones Place (sheet 8 already labels it Jones Place).
Riveredge Road is "River Edge Road" in OpenStreetMap; South Vivyen Street south of Harcourt Avenue is "Vivyen Street".
West Main Street meets North Prospect Avenue offset from its continuation east; those junctions were left out, as were duplicate modern nodes for South Queen and South Vivyen at West Main Street.
Two cinder-block buildings stand near West Main Street at North Prospect Avenue.
100 ft. West: Riveredge Rd to Vreeland Av, N./S. Queen to N./S. Prospect; Graphic Blvd grid, mostly vacant.

sheet-11-1.description: Sheet 11, part 1, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the west-central part of Bergenfield from West Church Street at the top to Anderson Avenue at the bottom, between North and South Prospect Avenue on the west and South Front Street on the east. The north end holds the town's institutions: Franklin High School, a brick building on a large lot between North Prospect Avenue and North Franklin Avenue, and the South Presbyterian Church, of concrete block with a wooden steeple, just north of West Church Street; a hall stands on North Franklin Avenue and an auto repair garage of concrete block (capacity 10 cars) on West Church Street beside a brook. The brook runs south from a pond at the top of the sheet, past Tyson Place and Van Houten Street, to Froelich Street. Below West Main Street the sheet is closely built with small frame dwellings on narrow lots along South Franklin Avenue, Haring Street, Coleman, Turnure, Vreeland and Sugden streets, Roosevelt Avenue, South Demarest Avenue, Bedford, Delford and Arlington avenues, with a few brick-veneered, tile and concrete-block houses. West Clinton Avenue crosses the lower third diagonally east of Roosevelt Avenue; a row of three concrete-block stores with a gasoline tank stands at its bend, and a workshop and a cement block building lie near Terrace Street. South of West Clinton Avenue, Henry Street, Melrose Avenue, Garden Street and Terrace run down to Anderson Avenue. Much of the south-west, along South Prospect Avenue, is still vacant lots. A fire alarm box stands at North Prospect Avenue and West Church Street. The top right corner of the sheet holds a separate inset (part 2).
notes: Van Houten Street west of the brook is now Meyns Place; Froelich Street between Haring Street and Roosevelt Avenue is now Fox Place.
The eastern block of Vreeland Avenue (east of the jog near South Prospect Avenue) is now Sunset Place.
South Demarest Avenue is "Demarest Avenue" in OpenStreetMap south of Van Houten Street.
The fitted rotation of this sheet is about -5 degrees, against about -0.5 on sheets 8 to 10; the junctions fit consistently, so the sheet is drawn turned on the page.
Franklin High School and the South Presbyterian Church are at the top of the sheet.

100 ft, drawn turned about 5 degrees. West-centre: W. Church to Anderson Av, Prospect to S. Front; Franklin High School. Part 2: boxed inset top right, Cleveland/W. Church between N. Demarest and Ralph.

sheet-11-2.description: Sheet 11, part 2 is an inset in the top right corner of the sheet, boxed off by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It shows the block between Cleveland Street and West Church Street from North Demarest Avenue east to Ralph Street, the piece of town that lies just south of sheet 9 and north of sheet 4. Cleveland Street forms the north side and West Church Street the south. A row of frame dwellings with garages, mostly two-storey, fronts Cleveland Street, with lots numbered from 40 down to 24 along it and block number 63; the south half of the block, toward West Church Street, is largely open. Six-inch water pipes run in Cleveland Street, North Demarest Avenue, West Church Street and Ralph Street, and a double hydrant stands at Ralph Street and West Church Street. The sheet's title cartouche (September 1928, Bergenfield, N.J.) is printed over the middle of the block. The inset is drawn turned about five degrees, like the main part of the sheet.
notes: Placed by its four corner junctions; the detector at first paired the north edge of Cleveland Street with a line beyond it and the bootstrap positions were re-read on close crops.

100 ft, drawn turned about 5 degrees. West-centre: W. Church to Anderson Av, Prospect to S. Front; Franklin High School. Part 2: boxed inset top right, Cleveland/W. Church between N. Demarest and Ralph.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the south-west corner of Bergenfield from West Clinton Avenue at the top down past Hallberg Avenue, between the Borough of New Milford line (a stream along the west edge) and South Prospect Avenue, with a strip east of South Prospect Avenue. The northern half is a dense small-lot development: South Queen Street and South Vivyen Street cross West Clinton Avenue, Levett, Somers and Cole avenues, and blocks 22 to 30 are cut into hundreds of narrow numbered lots, with rows of small frame dwellings and garages, a few concrete-block houses and one brick-veneered house. The Prospect Fire Co. No. 1 house stands on West Clinton Avenue near South Vivyen Street beside a small woodworking shop, and a store block of brick and concrete block faces South Prospect Avenue at Anderson Avenue. The southern half, below Cole Avenue, is laid out in large lots along Gingras Avenue, Hallberg Avenue and Van Valkenburgh Avenue, mostly vacant, with scattered frame dwellings and the Victory Cottage near South Prospect Avenue. East of South Prospect Avenue are Homestead Place, Park Road, West Broad Street, Whitman Street, Highview Avenue and Fairview Avenue, with blocks 118 and 119 platted into narrow lots and only a few houses. The bottom of the sheet (block 38) is open ground. Six-inch water pipes run in most streets and an eight-inch pipe in South Prospect Avenue; fire alarm boxes stand at South Vivyen Street and Levett Avenue and at South Prospect Avenue near Hallberg Avenue.
notes: Levett Avenue is now Levitt Avenue; Gingras Avenue is now Spring Avenue; Cole Avenue is Cole Street; West Clinton Avenue west of South Vivyen Street is "Clinton Avenue" in OpenStreetMap; West Broad Street meets South Prospect Avenue at the node named Broad Street.
The junctions along West Clinton Avenue at South Vivyen Street and South Prospect Avenue fit 6.6 and 10.9 m off and were rejected; the street appears to have been widened or realigned.
Park Road was not found in OpenStreetMap.
Prospect Fire Co. No. 1 house and the Victory Cottage are on this sheet.
100 ft. South-west: W. Clinton to Hallberg Av, New Milford line to S. Prospect; Levett, Somers, Cole, Gingras.

sheet-13-1.description: Sheet 13, part 1, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the south-central part of Bergenfield below Anderson Avenue, between South Prospect Avenue (just off the west edge) and the West Shore Railroad on the east. The top half is a grid of narrow numbered lots on blocks 109 to 124: Henry Street, Melrose Avenue, Garden Street, Terrace Street, Roosevelt Avenue, South Demarest Avenue, Arlington Avenue and South Front Street run south from Anderson Avenue, crossed by Homestead Place, Park Road, Bridge Street, Lake Street and Westside Avenue. They are lined with small frame dwellings and garages, with a scattering of concrete-block, brick-veneered and tile houses and a couple of small stores. Galloway Lumber & Supply Co., with an office and lumber shed, occupies a long strip beside the railroad south of South Front Street. Below Westside Avenue, West Broad Street crosses the sheet, with lot rows on blocks 122, 128 and 129 and Woodbine Street running south along the railroad lots of block 130. The south-west quarter, along Highview Avenue, Fairview Avenue, Luke Avenue and Whitman Street (blocks 118 and 119), is platted in long narrow lots, mostly vacant, with a few frame dwellings and a pair of stores on West Broad Street at Luke Avenue. Six-inch water pipes run in most streets; a fire alarm box stands at West Broad Street and Roosevelt Avenue. Two separately boxed insets occupy the lower right of the sheet (parts 2 and 3).
notes: Roosevelt Avenue south of Westside Avenue is also labelled Terrace Avenue in parentheses; the Roosevelt Avenue / West Broad Street junction fits 9.6 m off and was rejected.
South Demarest Avenue is "Demarest Avenue" in OpenStreetMap; West Broad Street meets Fairview and Highview avenues at nodes named Broad Street.
Park Road was not found in OpenStreetMap.
The sheet is drawn turned about five degrees (fitted rotation -4.7), as is sheet 11.
Galloway Lumber & Supply Co. is on this sheet.

100 ft, main part turned about 5 degrees. South-centre: Anderson Av to Whitman, Henry to S. Front; Galloway Lumber. Part 2: boxed inset S. Washington Av, Newbridge Rd to Liberty Rd (Teaneck line). Part 3: boxed inset Newbridge Coal & Supply Co. at the railroad.

sheet-13-2.description: Sheet 13, part 2 is a boxed inset in the lower middle of the sheet, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow, showing the southern tip of Bergenfield along South Washington Avenue between Newbridge Road and the Teaneck Township line. South Washington Avenue, with a 24-inch water main, runs down the inset and becomes Teaneck Road at the bottom, where Liberty Road branches off to the east along the borough line (marked City Limits, with Teaneck Township beyond). Warren Street meets Newbridge Road at the top left, where block 159 carries a row of frame dwellings. The rest of the inset is large open tracts (blocks 405 and 347) with a few frame dwellings and outbuildings. At the Liberty Road corner stand an auto repair shop of concrete block with gasoline tanks, a frame dwelling with a store, a small store with an oil house, and further east a frame building and a chicken coop.
notes: Newbridge Road is "New Bridge Road" in OpenStreetMap.

Placed as a two-point helmert at the atlas scale: the detected Newbridge Road / South Washington Avenue junction and a derived point 300 ft south along the drawn avenue, on the modern bearing of South Washington Avenue. The three-point fit first used (with Newbridge Road / Warren Street and Liberty Road) was internally inconsistent by about 13 degrees and sheared the inset; Newbridge Road has probably been realigned near Washington Avenue.
The borough line with Teaneck Township is drawn across the foot of the inset.

100 ft, main part turned about 5 degrees. South-centre: Anderson Av to Whitman, Henry to S. Front; Galloway Lumber. Part 2: boxed inset S. Washington Av, Newbridge Rd to Liberty Rd (Teaneck line). Part 3: boxed inset Newbridge Coal & Supply Co. at the railroad.

sheet-13-3.description: Sheet 13, part 3 is a small boxed inset in the lower right corner of the sheet, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow, showing the yard of the Newbridge Coal & Supply Co. on the west side of the West Shore Railroad, north of Newbridge Road. A siding curves off the main tracks into the yard, which holds concrete coal pockets, a small storage building, a garage and an office near the road. Newbridge Road crosses the foot of the inset and stops at the edge of the tracks. The rest of the inset is open ground.
notes: Placed on a single point, the crossing of New Bridge Road with the West Shore Railroad (River Subdivision in OpenStreetMap), with the scale assumed at 4.0 px/ft and the rotation taken from the measured lines; a derived second point carries no independent information. Low confidence.
Newbridge Coal & Supply Co. coal pockets and siding are on this inset.

100 ft, main part turned about 5 degrees. South-centre: Anderson Av to Whitman, Henry to S. Front; Galloway Lumber. Part 2: boxed inset S. Washington Av, Newbridge Rd to Liberty Rd (Teaneck line). Part 3: boxed inset Newbridge Coal & Supply Co. at the railroad.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers the southern part of Bergenfield on both sides of South Washington Avenue, at 100 feet to an inch, from West and East Broad at the top to Sylvan Avenue and Newbridge Road at the bottom. The West Shore Railroad runs down the west edge. West of South Washington Avenue are School, Elm, Miller and North streets, with McDermott Place, Hill Place, Foster and Warren running south; much of this side is open ground in large tracts (blocks 136, 137, 143, 153 and 156), with frame dwellings in the blocks at the top and around McDermott Place, Hill Place, Foster and Warren. East of the avenue a newer residential development is laid out in narrow lots: Carnation, Magnolia, Tulip and Lilac run east to Murray Hill Terrace, and south of Englewood Avenue the streets Beechwood, Linwood, Murray Hill (Greenwood) and Redwood run down to Sylvan Avenue. The blocks between Carnation and Tulip are closely built with two-storey frame dwellings and garages; those south of Tulip are almost entirely platted but empty lots. A creek winds along the east edge. Industry is sparse: the Independent Quilting Co. works (quilting and machine shop) on Newbridge Road near Foster, a small C.B. manufactory east of Washington Avenue, and an auto repairing garage on the west side of Washington Avenue. Water pipes, 24-inch on Washington Avenue and 6-inch on the cross streets, and fire alarm boxes and hydrants are marked. The scale bar is printed in Sylvan Avenue at the bottom.
notes: The street between blocks 335/336 and 340/341 is lettered Murray Hill with (Greenwood) south of Englewood Avenue; today it is all Murray Hill Terrace.
Englewood Avenue is drawn only east of South Washington Avenue; west of it the McDermott Place and Hill Place blocks end at a lot line, so those modern junctions were left out.
New Bridge Road / Warren Street was left out: the detector paired Newbridge Road's edge with another line at the sheet's bottom edge (5.6 m).
Independent Quilting Co. works on Newbridge Road; a C.B. manufactory east of South Washington Avenue.
100 ft. South Washington Avenue from West/East Broad to Sylvan Avenue and Newbridge Road; east side Carnation to Redwood and Murray Hill Terrace (new development); one part.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers the north-east of Bergenfield east of the Washington Avenue sheets, at 100 feet to an inch, from the Dumont borough line along the top (marked "See Map of Dumont") south to East Church Street. The upper half is a gridiron development of long, narrow numbered lots: New Jersey Avenue, New York Avenue, Merritt Avenue and Phelps Avenue run east from Leonard to beyond 2nd Street, crossed by 1st and 2nd streets. Most of these lots are still empty, with a scatter of frame dwellings and garages. At the west, East Kipp Street meets Leonard, and Tuscarora Street ends against a curved street that sweeps round from Merritt Avenue to East Central Avenue. The lower half is more closely built: East Central Avenue, Kuggas Place (a loop off Hickory Avenue), Hickory Avenue, Fahrner Street with McKinley Place, and East Johnson Avenue, crossed by Bond, North Taylor, Esser Place, Linden Place and Jagoe, are lined with two-storey frame dwellings, many with garages. At the bottom left, North William and North Summit end in turning circles above East Church Street, and Carol Lane runs down to it; many dwellings here are brick-veneered. The Svenska Evangelical Lutheran Church stands on East Johnson Avenue at North Taylor. A carpenter shop is near Linden Place. The south-east is a large empty tract (block 230) bounded by Jagoe and Martin Place. Six-inch and eight-inch water pipes run in Merritt, Phelps, East Central, Hickory and East Johnson avenues.
notes: Leonard is now Slater Street; East Kipp Street is Kipp Avenue.
North William and North Summit, drawn here as dead ends with turning circles north of East Church, are now Bell Place and Raum Place.
Bond is matched to the modern Violet Court (the junction with Hickory Avenue fits at 0.7 m).
Martin Place is now Martin Street; Jagoe, drawn from East Johnson Avenue north-east, no longer reaches East Johnson Avenue.
The Merritt Avenue / Phelps Avenue junction (the curved street at the west) and New Jersey Avenue / Slater Street (detected 7 m off at the corner of the sheet) were left out.
Svenska Evangelical Lutheran Church on East Johnson Avenue at North Taylor.
100 ft. North-east: New Jersey, New York, Merritt, Phelps, East Central, Hickory, East Johnson between Leonard (Slater) and 2nd Street; Dumont line at top; one part.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 covers the north-east corner of Bergenfield, at 100 feet to an inch, from the Dumont borough line along the top ("See Map of Dumont", with Maple Street lettered at the top right) to East Johnson Avenue and the edge of East Church Street at the bottom, and from 3rd Street and Martin Place east to the Tenafly borough line. The upper half is a speculative subdivision of narrow numbered lots: New Jersey and New York avenues west of Walnut, and Sycamore and Laburnum roads east of it, with a fan of wedge-shaped lots where Walnut meets the borough line. Below it Merritt, Phelps and Hickory avenues run east to Chestnut, crossed by 3rd, 4th, Oak Place and Clover; the blocks between Merritt and Phelps carry scattered frame dwellings and garages, with a store and a fire alarm on Merritt Avenue at 4th Street. South of Hickory Avenue the Thomas Jefferson School, a cinder-block building faced with brick with classrooms in two wings and an auditorium, stands in block 435 between Martin Place and Oak Place. Bogert Place and Whittaker Place run south from Hickory Avenue past East Johnson Avenue, which has a row of new two-storey dwellings east of Whittaker. Much of the east and south is open land in large tracts (blocks 195, 196A, 213, 214, 217 and 232 to 234). A creek runs along the east edge, and the Tenafly borough line crosses the sheet near it. Six-inch water pipes are marked in Merritt, Phelps, Hickory and Chestnut.
notes: Sycamore Road and Laburnum Road are the modern New Jersey Avenue and New York Avenue east of the old Walnut; Walnut itself was not built (the modern Minko Place and Shelley Court lie elsewhere).
The upper part of Clover (Phelps Avenue to beyond the lots) is the modern Pabis Lane; Martin Place is Martin Street.
4th Street jogs about 100 ft south of Phelps Avenue on the sheet but at Phelps Avenue today, so both 4th Street / Phelps Avenue junctions were left out.
Oak Place / Hickory Avenue fits 5.4 m off (modern Oak Place probably not on the old line) and was left out; Chestnut Street does not reach Hickory Avenue as drawn (rejected, 11 m).
Thomas Jefferson School, block 435.
100 ft. North-east corner: Sycamore and Laburnum roads, Merritt to East Johnson, 3rd Street to Chestnut and the Tenafly line; Thomas Jefferson School; one part.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 covers the residential blocks east of Washington Avenue in the centre of Bergenfield, at 100 feet to an inch, from East Church Street at the top to East Clinton Avenue at the bottom, and from George and the William streets east to North and South Christie. The east-west streets are Bradley Avenue, East Main Street, Grove, Palisade Avenue, Bergen Avenue and Madison Avenue; the north-south streets are North and South William, North and South Summit, North and South Taylor, North and South Woodside, 1st Street, Hudson, Jagoe, Christie, James and Elizabeth, with Carol Lane at the top and the stubs of Murray Hill Terrace, Beucler Place, Brook, View and Orchard streets below East Clinton Avenue. Most blocks are closely built with two-storey frame dwellings and garages, some brick-veneered or tile; the blocks east of 1st Street between Bradley Avenue and East Main Street are subdivided into narrow lots and largely empty. Public buildings: the Alert Fire Co. No. 1 fire department on North William Street at Bradley Avenue, and Public School No. 1, the Washington School, a brick building with a manual training room, on the north side of Palisade Avenue between South Summit and South Taylor. A public garage for eleven cars stands on North Summit Street near East Main Street, and there are a few small stores. The south-east is open land in large tracts (blocks 272, 279, 439 and 440). Six-inch water pipes run in most streets, with an eight-inch main in East Clinton Avenue.
notes: Elizabeth is now Hughes Road (its junctions with Bergen and Madison avenues fit at 2.0 and 0.9 m).
George is now Legion Drive. North William north of East Church is Bell Place and North Summit north of it is Raum Place.
The 1st Street / Bergen Avenue junction was left out (the modern node, shared with 1st Road, fits 5 m off).
Alert Fire Co. No. 1 (fire department) on North William Street; Public School No. 1, Washington School, on Palisade Avenue.
100 ft. East-centre: East Church to East Clinton, William to Christie; Washington School (Public School No. 1), Alert Fire Co. No. 1; one part.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers the south-east of Bergenfield on the Tenafly borough line, at 100 feet to an inch, from the end of East Church Street at the top to East Clinton Avenue at the bottom, and from North and South Christie east to the borough line. In the north-west, Bradley Avenue and East Main Street run between North Christie, Martin and Willett through blocks of narrow numbered lots, mostly unbuilt; Bogert Place, Martin Place and East Church Street end at the top edge. East Main Street turns south-east across the middle of the sheet towards Tenafly, with Bush, Cedar and Willow meeting it and Pine linking Cedar and Willow above it; the blocks here hold scattered dwellings, shanties, sheds and two greenhouses. Grove runs east from South Christie to Bush. The southern half is a newer development laid out east of Haven Avenue: Palisade, Bergen and Madison avenues cross Haven, Towne Place, Lodge Terrace and Lincoln Avenue, with Clyde Court and Lunn Avenue to the east; a row of new two-storey dwellings lines Bergen Avenue, and most of the rest is platted but empty. West of Haven Avenue a large open tract (blocks 280 to 282) holds the Rosehaven School, a frame building in block 281, and a few dwellings. A range of greenhouses stands north of Palisade Avenue near Towne Place. Cherry and Seminary streets leave East Clinton Avenue at the bottom. Six-inch water pipes run in East Main and Grove, and an eight-inch main in East Clinton Avenue.
notes: East of Haven Avenue, Palisade, Bergen and Madison avenues are now Preston Place, Galvan Place and Huber Place (their junctions fit at 1 to 4 m).
Pine is matched to the modern Davis Drive: its junction with Willow fits at 4.5 m but the one with Cedar was rejected (11 m), so the match is uncertain.

Bogert Place south of East Church Street and the East Main Street / Lincoln Avenue junction were left out; East Clinton Avenue / Lunn Avenue and East Clinton Avenue / Seminary Street were rejected (6 to 7 m).
Rosehaven School, block 281; greenhouses north of Palisade Avenue and south of East Main Street.
100 ft. South-east on the Tenafly line: Bradley, East Main, Grove, Haven Avenue development (Palisade, Bergen, Madison east of Haven), Lincoln, Lunn; Rosehaven School; one part.

sheet-19-1.description: The upper part of Sheet 19, at 100 feet to an inch, covers the residential blocks south of East Clinton Avenue in south-east Bergenfield, from Smith Avenue east to Orchard Street and from East Clinton Avenue south to East Broad and Highland Avenue. It is separated from the lower part of the sheet by a heavy line. In the west, Smith Avenue, Murray Hill Terrace, Beucler Place and Brook run south from East Clinton Avenue, with Edward Street and O'Neil Street leaving Smith Avenue westward and East Broad crossing at the bottom; these blocks are closely built with two-storey frame dwellings and garages, several of them tile or brick-veneered. A brick apartment building, drawn from plans, stands on Murray Hill Terrace near East Clinton Avenue, and there is a small store on Beucler Place. East of Brook lies a large open tract (block 291) and, below it, block 316. In the east a newer development is laid out between View and Orchard streets: Porter Avenue, Hillside Avenue, Pleasant Avenue and Highland Avenue, lined with narrow lots and many new dwellings. Block 323 below East Broad, at the bottom of this part, holds a row of new dwellings. Six-inch water pipes run in most streets, with an eight-inch main in East Clinton Avenue. The north arrow points nearly straight up.
notes: Smith Avenue / O'Neil Street and Smith Avenue / Edward Street were not detected; the west part rests on East Clinton Avenue and East Broad junctions.
Apartment building (brick, drawn from plans) on Murray Hill Terrace near East Clinton Avenue.
100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 Smith Avenue to Orchard Street, East Clinton to East Broad/Highland; part 2 (below) Orchard Street east to the Tenafly line, East Clinton to Highland.

sheet-19-2.description: The lower part of Sheet 19, below a heavy line across the sheet, is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and continues the south-east development east of Orchard Street, from East Clinton Avenue (whose north side is on Sheet 18) south to Highland Avenue and east to the Tenafly borough line. Porter Avenue, Hillside Avenue, Pleasant Avenue and Highland Avenue run east from Orchard Street across Cherry Street and Seminary to the borough line, which cuts the east ends of the blocks at a slant. The blocks (294 to 311) are platted in long rows of narrow numbered lots, most of them still empty, with a scatter of new two-storey frame dwellings and garages along East Clinton Avenue, Porter Avenue and Pleasant Avenue and a store on East Clinton Avenue near Cherry Street. South of Highland Avenue are large open tracts (blocks 318 to 320) with a few dwellings and a store. Orchard Street continues south of Pleasant Avenue. Six-inch water pipes run in Orchard, Seminary, Porter, Hillside and Pleasant; East Clinton Avenue carries an eight-inch main. The scale bar is printed below Highland Avenue at the bottom right.
notes: Orchard south of Pleasant Avenue is now Orchard Road.
This part is the eastward continuation of the upper part, drawn below it on the same sheet; Orchard Street is the seam between them.
100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 Smith Avenue to Orchard Street, East Clinton to East Broad/Highland; part 2 (below) Orchard Street east to the Tenafly line, East Clinton to Highland.
